news.headline: Aggies suspend 3 football players indefinitely, sources said
news.description: Texas A&M defensive back Denver Harris, receiver Chris Marshall and offensive lineman PJ Williams have been suspended indefinitely for violating team rules, sources told ESPN on Tuesday.

news.headline: Emotional Greg Schiano authors 'special' win, Rutgers' first at PSU since 1988
news.description: Less than two weeks removed from Rutgers announcing embattled Greg Schiano would return as coach for a 19th season, the Scarlet Knights stunned Penn State 25-24 Saturday, their first win over the Nittany Lions since 1988, and just their third this year.

news.headline: Notre Dame loses safety Luke Talich to injury in first quarter vs. SMU
news.description: Notre Dame starting safety Luke Talich left the Fighting Irish's game against SMU in the first quarter with an apparent right leg injury suffered on the opening drive of the game Saturday night in South Bend, Indiana.

news.headline: Brandon's two TD runs lift No. 9 Tennessee past LSU
news.description: Tennessee's stifling defense shut down LSU, and the No. 9 Volunteers beat the Tigers 27-13 on Saturday to maintain their place in the College Football Playoff hunt.

news.headline: Bryce Underwood makes most of second chance, sparks Michigan's upset of UCLA
news.description: Reinserted as Michigan's starting quarterback earlier this week, Bryce Underwood threw a 3-yard 2-point conversion pass Jalen Hoffman, lifting the Wolverines to an 18-16 triple-overtime win over previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA on Saturday night.

news.headline: Nebraska's jab at Ohio State's 'THE' leads top Week 12 CFB trolls
news.description: Nebraska deployed a simple but effective troll that poked fun at its opponent's propensity to emphasize the "the" in "The Ohio State University."

news.headline: Indiana's CFP hopes take hit after OT loss at Washington
news.description: Indiana might not get a chance to defend its national championship after losing 27-24 at Washington on Saturday.

news.headline: UCLA loses Ty Dieffenbach to injury, stays resolute with B1G title game in reach
news.description: UCLA coach Bob Chesney said his message to the Bruins was, "Nobody hang your head," despite losing QB Ty Dieffenbach to injury in a tough, 18-16 defeat at Michigan on Saturday.

wiki.title: P. J. Williams (offensive lineman)
wiki.intro: Patrick "P. J." Williams Jr. (born May 4, 2004) is an American college football offensive tackle for the SMU Mustangs. He previously played for the Texas A&M Aggies.

sections.title: Early life
sections.text:
Williams attended Dickinson High School in Dickinson, Texas, where he excelled in football. After learning to play on the offensive line as a sophomore, he was a three-time first-team all-district selection at the offensive tackle position. As a senior, Williams helped Dickinson go undefeated in district play and reach the second round of the state playoffs. He was named a Class 6A second-team all-state selection by the Texas Sports Writers Association (TSWA) and earned an invite to the 2022 Under Armour All-America Game. Aside from football, Williams also played basketball at Dickinson. He averaged 12.8 points and 6.9 rebounds per game as a senior.
Williams was rated as a consensus four-star recruit. He was ranked by 247Sports as the No. 9 prospect in the state of Texas in the class of 2022. On January 21, 2021, Williams verbally committed to playing college football at Texas A&M University over offers such as Houston, LSU, Michigan, Penn State, SMU, Texas, and Texas Tech. He signed with the Aggies in December.

sections.title: College career
sections.text:
Williams appeared in one game for the Aggies in 2022 and was redshirted. He was suspended from the team indefinitely in October for violating team rules, along with multiple teammates, reportedly due to a postgame locker room incident following a loss to South Carolina. On December 2, 2022, Williams announced he would be entering the NCAA transfer portal. He was rated as a three-star transfer recruit by Rivals.com and 247Sports. Williams went on official visits to Colorado, Houston, and SMU. On January 10, 2023, it was announced that he would transfer to SMU to play for the Mustangs.
In 2023, Williams appeared in 12 games, being employed both as a tackle and a guard. He made four starts at left tackle in relief of Marcus Bryant, including in the American Athletic Conference championship game. In 2024, Williams started all 14 games for the Mustangs, mostly at right tackle. He garnered third-team all-Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) honors. Williams was named one of six team captains for the 2025 season. He started 12 games for the Mustangs, earning second-team all-ACC accolades. Williams was named a captain again ahead of the 2026 season. He was also moved back to left tackle.
